Jonas, team — technical triage update. Summary of findings so far:

1) Root cause (preliminary): a short-lived route propagation delay between us-west-2 inter-region gateway and our control-plane router caused an overlap window in which traffic remained pinned to a draining backend pool. That coincided with an aggressive warm-pool drain triggered by an autoscaler event. The combination produced increased latency and higher 5xx for sessions that hit partially drained instances.

2) Why failover did not trigger immediately: our cross-region routing policy depends on a control-plane evaluation that uses aggregated health from both active and warm pools. During the overlap the health signals were noisy; a threshold check prevented automatic failover for ~12 minutes.

3) Mitigation completed at 09:10 PT:
- Increased route weight for us-east-1 to force traffic shift for in-flight checks
- Paused autoscaler warm-pool draining and restored instance weights
- Patch applied to control-plane threshold logic to reduce sensitivity to transient BGP flaps (hotfix id INF-4523)

Attachments uploaded: redwood-logs-usw2-20260511.zip, failover-diagram-v2.png (contain packet captures, route table dumps, and the decision flow chart).

Next steps (24-72 hours):
- Postmortem write-up with timeline and corrective actions (ownership: infra reliability)
- Config change to routing threshold and longer cool-down for warm-pool drains (scheduled deploy INF-4523)
- Run a controlled failover drill for customers on Reserved/Dedicated plans next week (ops + CS coordination)

I'll add more logs to the incident ticket and share the postmortem draft within 48 hours.

-Rishi
